description_full: Regency Centers Corporation is a pre-eminent national owner, operator, and developer of shopping centers located in suburban trade areas with compelling demographics. Our portfolio includes thriving properties merchandised with highly productive grocers, restaurants, service providers, and best-in-class retailers that connect to their neighborhoods, communities, and customers. Operating as a fully integrated real estate company, Regency Centers is a qualified real estate investment trust (REIT) that is self-administered, self-managed, and an S&P 500 Index member. Regency Centers Corporation was incorporated in 1963 and is based in Jacksonville, Florida.
ceo_bio: Ms. Lisa  Palmer | President, CEO & Director | Compensation: $4.0M (FY2025)
culture_narrative: Employs approximately 503 people. Revenue per employee of $3.1M ranks in the above the sector median among Real Estate peers, with revenue growing 5%/yr across its filed history. Stock-based compensation of $39K per employee reflects an ownership culture. CEO compensation is 1× revenue per employee (modest relative to workforce productivity). Governance score flags low compensation governance risk (1/10).
financial_summary: Regency Centers Corporation is a large-cap real estate business with a $14.2B market cap on $1.6B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +8% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 6% against a 7% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 3.1× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and interest coverage runs at 6.3×.

Shareholder yield of 2.9% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and within its sector the business captures 3.6× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

sect: Its 72% operating margin runs 50pp above the Real Estate median (23%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
It captures 3.65x its revenue share in sector profits, taking a disproportionate slice of the profit pool.

Over five years it has been gaining share of the sector profit pool (+29.3% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 146 companies in the universe; the top four hold 25% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares have drifted higher, up 7% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 9% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 16% and a beta of 0.69, it is more defensive than the market, though its beta has shifted (1y -0.04 vs 5y 0.65), so read it loosely.
About $93.4M trades a day, enough to build a position.
In past sell-offs it fell 49% in the 2020 crash, 30% in the 2022 bear market and 68% in 2008.
val: The price sits above its blended-model fair value of $33.96 (margin of safety -124%), so there is no valuation cushion.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 31%), so treat the estimate as noisy.
Against its own history it is cheap: the EBIT multiple sits 47% below its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are thin: an EBIT/EV of 5.8% (vs the 8% bar).
The 18 covering analysts target $84.56 on average, 11% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 6% falls short of the cost of capital of 7.4%, so growth at these returns destroys value; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.50).
Earnings quality looks solid: cash conversion of 1.57x.
AFFO margin (a proxy for distributable REIT cash) is 53%.
ROE of 8% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.9x equity multiplier).

It spends 1.3% of revenue on stock compensation.
hlth: Leverage is heavy at 3.1x net debt to EBITDA ($144.1M of cash against $4.7B of debt), with interest covered 6.3x.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 8.3% over 3 years and 8.9% over 5 years.
Free cash flow has compounded 10.6% a year over five years.
Forward indicators: FFO growth of 10.6% a year over five years.
own: Insiders hold little stock (0.6%), and reported institutional holdings exceed 100% of shares (a sign of heavy share lending).
Insiders have only sold over the past year (5 sales, net $22.3M sold).
It returns 2.9% a year to shareholders (4.2% in dividends, less 0.7% of net share issuance).
It pays out 108% of earnings, more than it earns, so the dividend is at risk.
people: With about 503 employees, each generates about $3.1M of revenue, 1.4x the Real Estate median, and revenue has grown 5.4% a year across its filed history.
CEO pay is $4.0M (1x revenue per employee), and compensation governance scores well (1/10, lower is better).
